record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: For integers k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1, what is the descriptive complexity of the set CPE^k(T^n) of C^k self-maps of the n-torus with completely positive entropy?

evidence.quote: Question 2.2 (García-Ramos). Let k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1. What is the complexity of CPEk(Πn)?
We say f ∈ Ck(X, X) has completely positive entropy if every non-trivial factor has positive topological entropy. We denote the set of such functions with CPEk(X).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ and $k \geq 1$ be integers, and let $\mathbb{T}^n = \mathbb{R}^n / \mathbb{Z}^n$ denote the $n$-dimensional torus. Equip the space $C^k(\mathbb{T}^n, \mathbb{T}^n)$ of $C^k$ self-maps of $\mathbb{T}^n$ with the standard $C^k$ topology, making it a Polish space.

For a continuous self-map $f : X \to X$ of a compact metric space, the topological entropy $h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$ is defined in the usual way. A topological factor of $(X,f)$ is a pair $(Y,g)$ with $g : Y \to Y$ continuous on a compact metric space together with a continuous surjection $\pi : X \to Y$ satisfying $\pi \circ f = g \circ \pi$. The factor is called trivial if $|Y| = 1$. The map $f$ is said to have completely positive entropy if every non-trivial topological factor of $(X,f)$ has strictly positive topological entropy.

Define
$$\mathrm{CPE}^k(\mathbb{T}^n) := \{ f \in C^k(\mathbb{T}^n, \mathbb{T}^n) : f \text{ has completely positive entropy} \}.$$

Determine the descriptive set-theoretic complexity of $\mathrm{CPE}^k(\mathbb{T}^n)$ as a subset of the Polish space $C^k(\mathbb{T}^n, \mathbb{T}^n)$. In particular, locate this set precisely within the Borel/projective hierarchy (e.g., determine whether it is Borel, and if not, whether it is complete coanalytic).
artifact.status_search_result: Related work by Darji and García-Ramos ("Local entropy theory and descriptive complexity", arXiv:2107.09263) shows that for many classes of compact spaces the set of dynamical systems with completely positive entropy is complete coanalytic (hence not Borel), with specific results for the circle, torus and certain compact orientable manifolds in the continuous category. The precise descriptive complexity of $\mathrm{CPE}^k(\mathbb{T}^n)$ within $C^k(\mathbb{T}^n,\mathbb{T}^n)$ for arbitrary $k \geq 1$ and $n \geq 1$ does not appear to have been fully resolved in the literature, and the question is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Local entropy theory and descriptive complexity
status_evidence.snippet: For a large class of compact spaces, the family of dynamical systems with CPE is complete coanalytic and hence not Borel. Results also hold for the circle, the torus and some other compact orientable manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes complete coanalyticity of CPE in the continuous setting on several manifolds, but the C^k case on the torus is not fully addressed.

status_evidence.title: Local entropy theory and applications (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of local entropy theory, including descriptive set-theoretic aspects of CPE.
status_evidence.claim: Survey context indicating ongoing investigation of descriptive complexity of CPE.
